To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the AUC0→4 monitoring of cyclospirone is a better indicator of the risk for acute rejection than recommended C0 or C2 values, 2) the AUC value is more closely related to the risk for acute rejections when the AUC is calculated from 0 to 4 h after the administration of the drug than when it is calculated from 1 h after administration of the drug (AUC1→4), 3) the AUC monitoring
AUC(0-12) and C(0-12)/C(0-4) values are more accurate than C(2) in identifying patients with a high risk of acute rejection after kidney transplantation.
The C0, C2 and AUC0-2 values are significantly higher in patients with acute rejection compared with patients who did not experience rejection.

the aim of this study was to determine the optimal C2 concentration and the best time to measure the C2 concentration for predicting the risk of acute rejection after kidney transplantation.

the aim of this study was to evaluate the ability of AUC(0-4) and C2 to detect acute rejection in kidney transplant patients during induction therapy with basiliximab and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) and cyclosporine (CsA).

the use of C2 monitoring in addition to trough monitoring of cyclosporing A (CsA) can be beneficial for patients who receive induction therapy with basiliximab and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF).
the use of C2 monitoring is not necessary to achieve adequate immunosuppression in the early post-transplant period.
